subject: DPA — OxyTech: privacy counsel comments on subprocessors & transfers
messages:
From: Julia Hart <julia.hart@oxytech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@oxytech.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OxyTech DPA - initial redlines (subprocessors, transfers, KMS)

Hi Monica,

Thanks for sending the standard DPA. Attached are our counsel's redlines (see attachment: OxyTech_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx). The key items for our security/privacy team are outlined below to give you visibility before we dive into line edits: 

- Subprocessors: OxyTech requires either explicit consent for new subprocessors or a 30-day notice with an approval step for critical categories (we've proposed an approval right for Category A services).
- International transfers: we insist on explicit SCCs for EU-to-US transfers for backups and logs, plus an option to switch to customer-controlled encryption for EU data at rest.
- Customer-managed keys (KMS): we have inserted language requiring bring-your-own-key (BYOK) when handling highly sensitive PII — this is a blocker for one of our regulated customers unless accommodated.
- Audit rights: on-site audit rights (with reasonable notice and NDA) for select data centers; we flagged SOC 2 as insufficient on its own.
- Retention & deletion: 90-day maximum for backups and a clear deletion/return window of 30 days post-termination.

We know some asks are aggressive; we are open to commercial compromises but need to surface these now. Can your privacy team review and let us know your positions by COB Wed (22 Apr)? Our procurement team is coordinating DocuSign once terms are agreed.

Thanks,
Julia Hart
Senior Counsel, OxyTech

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: OxyTech DPA - initial redlines (subprocessors, transfers, KMS)

Thanks for the ping — reviewed Julia's redlines and prepared a proposed approach below and in an attached redline. High-level positions we should take: 

1) Subprocessors: we should not grant categorical approval rights (veto) for new subprocessors. Counter: commit to 30 days' notice and an objection right limited to material security or compliance harms (and only for Category A: data hosting, KMS, logging). If OxyTech insists on approval, offer a one-time carveout for named subprocessors in the schedule.

2) Transfers & SCCs: accept SCCs for EU transfers and confirm adherence to EU SCCs + appropriate technical safeguards. For customer-controlled encryption (BYOK) — we can offer BYOK for Redwood Private deployments and select Dedicated configurations (where hardware supports HSM-backed keys). For hosted accounts we cannot offer BYOK at scale; propose enhanced encryption-in-transit and at-rest standard with region-locking for EU data.

3) KMS / BYOK: as above — offer BYOK only on Private or Dedicated dedicated pools with a commercial addendum and setup lead time (4–6 weeks). For hosted customers, we can offer bring-your-own-key for a premium managed key product, but by default Redwood manages keys. Require clear SLAs and operational runbook for key compromise scenarios in the addendum.

4) Audit rights: SOC 2 Type II + consolidated audit report is baseline. On-site audits are high-cost and operationally sensitive; counter with right to a mutually-agreed third-party assessment (at customer's expense) or a targeted document review plus an annual audit window. For on-site, require NDA and 45 days' notice and limit to specific instances tied to regulatory need.

5) Retention & deletion: agree to 30 days to delete customer data post-termination from active stores, backups retained up to 90 days. Offer a contractual option for shorter retention windows for regulated customers with a small fee.

6) Liability / indemnity: where the redlines expand risk (e.g., open approval rights or BYOK obligations that increase operational control), escalate to commercial/legal for price adjustments.

I attached a redline with specific phrasing (OxyTech_DPA_Redlines_v1_redline.docx). Key suggested text snippets included in the attachment; main changes are: narrow subprocessors objection right, BYOK limited-scope clause for Private/Dedicated, SCCs acceptance, and audit compromise language.

Recommend we push back on any unconditional BYOK requirement for hosted service and on on-site audit as a default. If OxyTech signals these are deal-breakers, we should propose a limited pilot with a separate addendum and cost recovery clause.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Julia — thanks for the clear summary and for surfacing the must-haves. We reviewed with privacy and commercial, and attached is our counter DPA (Redwood_OxyTech_DPA_Counter_v1.docx) with track changes. High level: 

- Accepted: SCCs for EU transfers; 30-day notice for subprocessors with a narrow objection right limited to material security or compliance harms; 30-day deletion from active systems, backups up to 90 days.
- Conditional / commercial: BYOK — we can support BYOK for Private and Dedicated Dedicated Pools with an addendum (one-time setup fee + 4–6 week lead time). For hosted accounts, BYOK is available as a managed add-on at additional cost.
- Audit: SOC 2 Type II signals accepted; for on-site audits we propose an alternative: a targeted third-party assessment or a documented evidence pack plus 45 days' notice. On-site audits would require an NDA and cost recovery.

If these positions are acceptable, I can send the DPA for signature via DocuSign. We included a DocuSign envelope link below for your convenience. Please review the attached redline and let us know any final comments by Mon (26 Apr) so we can meet your procurement target.

DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.example/envelope/ABC123-oxytech
